name: Hydroxyzine

lead: Hydroxyzine is an older prescription antihistamine used for anxiety, allergic itching and sedation around surgery.
No research links it to appearance outcomes; it is listed because of its sleep-aiding and anti-itch uses.

paras: It blocks histamine H1 receptors and, because it enters the brain, causes sedation.
Drowsiness, dry mouth and dizziness are common. Labels warn about combined sedation with alcohol, rare heart rhythm effects and seizures, and use in early pregnancy.

lead: Hydroxyzine is a first-generation antihistamine of the piperazine class, approved by the US FDA in 1956. Its US label covers symptomatic relief of anxiety and tension, itching from allergic conditions such as chronic urticaria and atopic or contact dermatitis, and sedation before and after general anaesthesia [1][2].

It appears in the wiki's recovery category because of its sedative and anti-itch uses. No studies were found on hydroxyzine for appearance outcomes, and no looksmaxxing community discussion was identified.
Reviews list it among treatments for anxiety disorders and for urticaria [3][4]. Its sedating effect is linked to its ability to cross into the brain [5].

paras: The US label for hydroxyzine pamoate lists anxiety and tension, allergic pruritus and sedative premedication among its indications [1][2]. A 2020 review of anxiety pharmacotherapy discusses it among off-label and approved options [3]. Urticaria guidance and reviews describe sedating antihistamines as a long-standing therapy for itch [4]. A pilot trial in interstitial cystitis tested hydroxyzine alongside pentosan polysulfate [6].

Common effects include drowsiness, dry mouth, dizziness and headache; the label and reviews warn of added sedation with alcohol and other central nervous system depressants, and of rare seizures or heart rhythm effects [1][2]. Use is contraindicated in early pregnancy per the label, and caution applies in older adults [1][2].

Hydroxyzine blocks histamine H1 receptors. A 2003 study found sedating H1 antagonists such as hydroxyzine are not limited by P-glycoprotein at the blood-brain barrier, unlike non-sedating antihistamines, which fits their central effects [5].

Registered trials include a strabismus surgery premedication study, a trial of itch prevention after spinal morphine and a pilot study with opioid withdrawal [7][8][9]. A trial of hydroxyzine for anxiety in people with eating disorders was withdrawn [10]. A 2003 pilot trial examined it in interstitial cystitis [6]. No studies were found on hydroxyzine for appearance outcomes.
